source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Hebrew. **THE MACCABEAN APOCALYPSE** — the longest sustained vaticinium-ex-eventu in the HB, providing detailed (and historically verifiable) overview of Hellenistic-period Near-Eastern history c. 333-164 BCE. SECONDARY: 4Q114 (Danielc) preserves substantial fragments — especially of vv 1-35, providing important verification. TERTIARY: OG-Greek + Theodotion-Greek consulted at the textually contested vv 17-20 (the marriage-alliance details) + vv 36-39 (the king-exalts-himself).
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999; 1 + 2 Macc; Polybius; Diodorus Siculus.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2; 1 Macc 1-6; 2 Macc 3-9.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 11 — HEBREW, the king-of-the-north vs king-of-the-south wars. The chapter is a sustained encoded narrative of Hellenistic-period history: Persian Empire decline (vv 1-2) → Alexander (vv 3-4) → Diadochi wars (vv 5-20, esp Ptolemies/Seleucids) → Antiochus IV Epiphanes (vv 21-45). **CRITICAL SCHOLARLY CONSENSUS** (Collins 1993, Newsom 2014, Hartman-DiLella 1978): vv 1-39 are detailed *vaticinia ex eventu* (history written as prophecy, dating the text to 167-164 BCE); vv 40-45 contain genuine (unfulfilled) prediction about Antiochus IV's final campaign — predictions that did NOT come true (Antiochus died in Persia of disease, not in a final invasion of Egypt), which dates the text precisely to the period between 167 (composition) and 164 (Antiochus's death). This is the foundational scholarly argument for Maccabean dating of Daniel. **CROSS-CORPUS**: 1 Macc 1; 2 Macc 3-9; Polybius 26-31; Diodorus Siculus 30-31 — all corroborate the historical events encoded in vv 21-39.

verses.text: וַאֲנִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֔ת לְדָרְיָ֖וֶשׁ הַמָּדִ֑י עָמְדִ֛י לְמַחֲזִ֥יק וּלְמָע֖וֹז לֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾănî bi-šnaṯ ʾaḥaṯ lə-Dāryāweš ham-Māḏî ʿomdî lə-maḥăzîq ū-lə-māʿōz lō
verses.notes: **'And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.'** Continues the angel's speech from ch 10. The speaker (Gabriel-figure) supported Darius the Mede — angelic support of Israel-favorable rulers.

verses.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה אֱמֶ֖ת אַגִּ֣יד לָ֑ךְ הִנֵּה־עוֹד֩ שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה מְלָכִ֜ים עֹמְדִ֣ים לְפָרַ֗ס וְהָֽרְבִיעִי֙ יַעֲשִׁ֤יר עֹֽשֶׁר־גָּדוֹל֙ מִכֹּ֔ל וּכְחֶזְקָת֣וֹ בְעָשְׁר֔וֹ יָעִ֣יר הַכֹּ֔ל אֵ֖ת מַלְכ֥וּת יָוָֽן׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿattāh ʾĕmeṯ ʾaggîḏ lāḵ hinnēh-ʿōḏ šəlōšāh məlāḵîm ʿōmḏîm lə-Pārās wə-hā-rəḇîʿî yaʿăšîr ʿōšer-gāḏōl mik-kōl ū-ḵə-ḥezqāṯō ḇə-ʿošrō yāʿîr hak-kōl ʾēṯ malḵūṯ Yāwān
verses.notes: **'And now I will show you the truth. Behold, three more kings shall arise in Persia; and a fourth shall be far richer than all of them; and when he has become strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the kingdom of Greece.'** **HISTORICAL IDENTIFICATION**: the three Persian kings after Cyrus = Cambyses II (530-522), Pseudo-Smerdis (522), Darius I (522-486). The fourth richest = Xerxes I (486-465), whose massive invasion of Greece (480-479 BCE) — Thermopylae, Salamis, Plataea — fits 'stir up all against Greece'. The intervening Persian kings (Artaxerxes I through Darius III) are skipped — the apocalyptic schematization.

verses.text: וְעָמַ֖ד מֶ֣לֶךְ גִּבּ֑וֹר וּמָשַׁל֙ מִמְשָׁ֣ל רַ֔ב וְעָשָׂ֖ה כִּרְצוֹנֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāmaḏ meleḵ gibbōr ū-māšal mimšāl raḇ wə-ʿāśāh ki-rṣōnō
verses.notes: **'Then a mighty king shall arise, who shall rule with great dominion and do according to his will.'** **= ALEXANDER THE GREAT** (336-323 BCE).

verses.text: וּכְעָמְדוֹ֙ תִּשָּׁבֵ֣ר מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְתֵחָ֕ץ לְאַרְבַּ֖ע רוּח֣וֹת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א לְאַחֲרִית֗וֹ וְלֹ֤א כְמָשְׁלוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָשָׁ֔ל כִּ֤י תִנָּתֵשׁ֙ מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְלַאֲחֵרִ֖ים מִלְּבַד־אֵֽלֶּה׃
verses.translit: ū-ḵə-ʿomḏō tiš-šāḇēr malḵūṯō wə-ṯē-ḥāṣ lə-ʾarbaʿ rūḥōṯ haš-šāmāyim wə-lōʾ lə-ʾaḥărîṯō wə-lōʾ ḵə-mošlō ʾăšer māšāl kî ṯinnāṯēš malḵūṯō wə-la-ʾăḥērîm mil-ləḇaḏ-ʾēlleh
verses.notes: **'And when he has arisen, his kingdom shall be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven, but not to his posterity, nor according to the dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom shall be plucked up and go to others besides these.'** Alexander's empire divided among the Diadochi (cf. 8:8, 8:22). Alexander's actual heir (Alexander IV) was murdered c. 309 BCE.

verses.text: וְיֶחֱזַ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־הַנֶּ֖גֶב וּמִן־שָׂרָ֑יו וְיֶחֱזַ֤ק עָלָיו֙ וּמָשָׁ֔ל מִמְשָׁ֥ל רַ֖ב מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-yeḥĕzaq meleḵ-han-neḡeḇ ū-min-śārāyw wə-yeḥĕzaq ʿālāyw ū-māšāl mimšāl raḇ memšaltō
verses.notes: **'Then the king of the south shall be strong, but one of his princes shall be stronger than he and rule, and his dominion shall be a great dominion.'** **'KING OF THE SOUTH' = PTOLEMAIC EGYPT**. The first king of the south = Ptolemy I Soter (323-285 BCE). 'One of his princes' = Seleucus I Nicator (founder of the Seleucid dynasty), originally one of Ptolemy's officers; Seleucus I (312-281 BCE) became the founder of the larger Seleucid Empire. **'KING OF THE NORTH' = SELEUCIDS**.

verses.text: וּלְקֵ֤ץ שָׁנִים֙ יִתְחַבָּ֔רוּ וּבַ֣ת מֶֽלֶךְ־הַנֶּ֗גֶב תָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת מֵישָׁרִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־תַעְצֹ֞ר כּ֣וֹחַ הַזְּר֗וֹעַ וְלֹ֤א יַעֲמֹד֙ וּזְרֹע֔וֹ וְתִנָּתֵ֨ן הִ֤יא וּמְבִיאֶ֙יהָ֙ וְהַיֹּ֣לְדָ֔הּ וּמַחֲזִקָ֖הּ בָּעִתִּֽים׃
verses.translit: ū-lə-qēṣ šānîm yiṯ-ḥabbārū ū-ḇaṯ meleḵ-han-neḡeḇ tāḇōʾ ʾel-meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn la-ʿăśōṯ mêšārîm wə-lōʾ-ṯaʿṣōr kōaḥ haz-zərōaʿ wə-lōʾ yaʿămōḏ ū-zərōʿō wə-ṯinnāṯēn hîʾ ū-məḇîʾêhā wə-hay-yōləḏāh ū-maḥăziqāh bā-ʿittîm
verses.notes: **'After some years they shall make an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north to make peace; but she shall not retain the strength of her arm, and he and his offspring shall not endure; but she shall be given up, and her attendants, her child, and he who got possession of her.'** **HISTORICAL FULFILLMENT**: Ptolemy II Philadelphus's daughter Berenice married Antiochus II Theos (252 BCE); Antiochus II divorced his first wife Laodice to marry Berenice. After Ptolemy II's death (246 BCE), Laodice's faction murdered Berenice + her son and Antiochus II — restoring Laodice's son Seleucus II to the throne. Polybius 5.40.

verses.text: וְעָמַ֛ד מִנֵּ֥צֶר שָׁרָשֶׁ֖יהָ כַּנּ֑וֹ וְיָבֹ֣א אֶל־הַחַ֗יִל וְיָבֹא֙ בְּמָעוֹז֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וְעָשָׂ֥ה בָהֶ֖ם וְהֶחֱזִֽיק׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāmaḏ min-nēṣer šorāšêhā kannō wə-yāḇōʾ ʾel-ha-ḥayil wə-yāḇōʾ bə-māʿōz meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn wə-ʿāśāh ḇā-hem wə-heḥĕzîq
verses.notes: **'In those times a branch from her roots shall arise in his place; he shall come against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north, and he shall deal with them and shall prevail.'** **= PTOLEMY III EUERGETES** (246-221 BCE), Berenice's brother, who invaded Seleucid territory in the Third Syrian War (246-241 BCE) to avenge his sister, reaching as far as Antioch and Babylon.

verses.text: וְגַ֣ם אֱֽלֹהֵיהֶ֡ם עִם־נְסִֽכֵיהֶם֩ עִם־כְּלֵ֨י חֶמְדָּתָ֜ם כֶּ֧סֶף וְזָהָ֛ב בַּשְּׁבִ֖י יָבִ֣א מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהוּא֙ שָׁנִ֣ים יַעֲמֹ֔ד מִמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַצָּפֽוֹן׃
verses.translit: wə-ḡam ʾĕlōhêhem ʿim-nəsiḵêhem ʿim-kəlê ḥemdāṯām kesep̄ wə-zāhāḇ baš-šəḇî yāḇiʾ Miṣrāyim wə-hūʾ šānîm yaʿămōḏ mim-meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn
verses.notes: **'He shall also carry off to Egypt their gods with their molten images and with their precious vessels of silver and gold; and for some years he shall refrain from attacking the king of the north.'** Ptolemy III seized Egyptian temple-images that had been carried away by Cambyses centuries earlier — celebrated in the Canopus Decree (238 BCE) and the Adulis Inscription.

verses.text: וּבָ֗א בְּמַלְכוּת֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֔גֶב וְשָׁ֖ב אֶל־אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇāʾ bə-malḵūṯ meleḵ han-neḡeḇ wə-šāḇ ʾel-ʾaḏmāṯō
verses.notes: **'Then the latter shall come into the realm of the king of the south but shall return into his own land.'** **= SELEUCUS II CALLINICUS** (246-225 BCE) attempted a counter-invasion of Egypt c. 240 BCE but was forced to retreat.

verses.text: ובנו וּבָנָ֣יו יִתְגָּר֗וּ וְאָסְפוּ֙ הֲמוֹן֙ חֲיָלִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וּבָ֥א ב֖וֹא וְשָׁטַ֣ף וְעָבָ֑ר וְיָשֹׁ֥ב ויתגרו וְיִתְגָּרֶ֖ה עַד־מָעֻזֹּֽה׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇānāyw yiṯgārū wə-ʾāsəp̄ū hămōn ḥăyālîm rabbîm ū-ḇāʾ ḇōʾ wə-šāṭap̄ wə-ʿāḇār wə-yāšōḇ wə-yiṯgāreh ʿaḏ-māʿuzzōh
verses.notes: **'His sons shall wage war and assemble a multitude of great forces, which shall come on and overflow and pass through; and they shall return and carry the war as far as his fortress.'** **= SELEUCUS III + ANTIOCHUS III THE GREAT**. Antiochus III (223-187 BCE) waged the Fourth Syrian War (219-217 BCE), invading Ptolemaic territory. Qere-ketiv: ובנו/וּבָנָיו; ויתגרו/וְיִתְגָּרֶה.

verses.text: וְיִתְמַרְמַר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֔גֶב וְיָצָ֕א וְנִלְחַ֥ם עִמּ֖וֹ עִם־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֑וֹן וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ הָמ֣וֹן רָ֔ב וְנִתַּ֥ן הֶהָמ֖וֹן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-yiṯmarmar meleḵ han-neḡeḇ wə-yāṣāʾ wə-nilḥam ʿimmō ʿim-meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn wə-heʿĕmîḏ hāmōn rāḇ wə-nittan he-hāmōn bə-yāḏō
verses.notes: **'Then the king of the south, moved with rage, shall come out and fight with the king of the north; and he shall raise a great multitude, but it shall be given into his hand.'** **= BATTLE OF RAPHIA** (217 BCE): Ptolemy IV Philopator defeated Antiochus III decisively. Polybius 5.79-86; 3 Macc 1.

verses.text: וְנִשָּׂ֥א הֶהָמ֖וֹן ירום וְרָ֣ם לְבָב֑וֹ וְהִפִּ֛יל רִבֹּא֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יָעֽוֹז׃
verses.translit: wə-niśśāʾ he-hāmōn wə-rām ləḇāḇō wə-hippîl ribbōʾōṯ wə-lōʾ yāʿōz
verses.notes: **'And when the multitude is taken away, his heart shall be exalted, and he shall cast down tens of thousands, but he shall not prevail.'** Ptolemy IV's victory at Raphia did not lead to permanent gains. Qere-ketiv: ירום/וְרָם.

verses.text: וְשָׁב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וְהֶעֱמִ֣יד הָמ֔וֹן רַ֖ב מִן־הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וּלְקֵ֨ץ הָֽעִתִּ֤ים שָׁנִים֙ יָ֣בוֹא ב֔וֹא בְּחַ֥יִל גָּד֖וֹל וּבִרְכ֥וּשׁ רָֽב׃
verses.translit: wə-šāḇ meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn wə-heʿĕmîḏ hāmōn raḇ min-hā-rîšōn ū-lə-qēṣ hā-ʿittîm šānîm yāḇōʾ ḇōʾ bə-ḥayil gāḏōl ū-ḇi-rḵūš rāḇ
verses.notes: **'For the king of the north shall again raise a multitude, greater than the former; and after some years he shall come on with a great army and abundant supplies.'** Antiochus III's Fifth Syrian War (202-198 BCE), his successful reconquest of Coele-Syria including Judea.

verses.text: וּבָעִתִּ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם רַבִּ֥ים יַֽעַמְד֖וּ עַל־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֑גֶב וּבְנֵ֣י ׀ פָּרִיצֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ יִֽנַּשְּׂא֛וּ לְהַעֲמִ֥יד חָז֖וֹן וְנִכְשָֽׁלוּ׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇā-ʿittîm hā-hēm rabbîm yaʿamḏū ʿal-meleḵ han-neḡeḇ ū-ḇənê pārîṣê ʿammə-ḵā yinnaśśəʾū lə-haʿămîḏ ḥāzōn wə-niḵšālū
verses.notes: **'In those times many shall rise against the king of the south; and the men of violence among your own people shall lift themselves up in order to fulfill the vision, but they shall fail.'** **'MEN OF VIOLENCE AMONG YOUR OWN PEOPLE'**: Hellenizing Jews aligning with Antiochus III against Ptolemaic rule. Josephus, Antiquities 12.129-134.

verses.text: וְיָבֹא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וְיִשְׁפֹּךְ֙ סֽוֹלֲלָ֔ה וְלָכַ֖ד עִ֣יר מִבְצָר֑וֹת וּזְרֹע֤וֹת הַנֶּ֙גֶב֙ לֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֔דוּ וְעַם֙ מִבְחָרָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין כֹּ֖חַ לַעֲמֹֽד׃
verses.translit: wə-yāḇōʾ meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn wə-yišpōḵ sōlălāh wə-lāḵaḏ ʿîr miḇṣārōṯ ū-zərōʿōṯ han-neḡeḇ lōʾ yaʿămōḏū wə-ʿam miḇḥārāyw wə-ʾên kōaḥ la-ʿămōḏ
verses.notes: **'Then the king of the north shall come and throw up siegeworks, and take a well-fortified city. And the forces of the south shall not stand, or even his picked troops, for there shall be no strength to stand.'** **= SIEGE OF SIDON** (198 BCE) following Battle of Panium (200 BCE) — Antiochus III's decisive victory.

verses.text: וְיַ֨עַשׂ הַבָּ֤א אֵלָיו֙ כִּרְצוֹנ֔וֹ וְאֵ֥ין עוֹמֵ֖ד לְפָנָ֑יו וְיַעֲמֹ֥ד בְּאֶֽרֶץ־הַצְּבִ֖י וְכָלָ֥ה בְיָדֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-yaʿaś hab-bāʾ ʾēlāyw ki-rṣōnō wə-ʾên ʿōmēḏ lə-p̄ānāyw wə-yaʿămōḏ bə-ʾereṣ-haṣ-ṣəḇî wə-ḵālāh ḇə-yāḏō
verses.notes: **'He who comes against him shall do according to his own will, and none shall stand before him; and he shall stand in the glorious land, and all of it shall be in his power.'** Antiochus III controls Judea ('the glorious land' — cf. 8:9, 11:41) c. 198 BCE.

verses.text: וְיָשֵׂ֣ם ׀ פָּ֠נָיו לָב֞וֹא בְּתֹ֧קֶף כָּל־מַלְכוּת֛וֹ וִישָׁרִ֥ים עִמּ֖וֹ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וּבַ֤ת הַנָּשִׁים֙ יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֔הּ וְלֹ֥א תַעֲמֹ֖ד וְלֹא־ל֥וֹ תִהְיֶֽה׃
verses.translit: wə-yāśēm pānāyw lā-ḇōʾ bə-ṯōqep̄ kol-malḵūṯō wî-šārîm ʿimmō wə-ʿāśāh ū-ḇaṯ han-nāšîm yitten-lō lə-hašḥîṯāh wə-lōʾ ṯaʿămōḏ wə-lōʾ-lō ṯihyeh
verses.notes: **'He shall set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and he shall bring terms of peace and perform them. He shall give him the daughter of women to destroy the kingdom; but it shall not stand or be to his advantage.'** **= ANTIOCHUS III'S MARRIAGE-ALLIANCE**: gave his daughter Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V Epiphanes (193 BCE) intending to use her to influence Egypt — but she sided with her husband against her father. Polybius 28.20.

verses.text: וישב וְיָשֵׂ֧ם ׀ פָּנָ֛יו לְאִיִּ֖ים וְלָכַ֣ד רַבִּ֑ים וְהִשְׁבִּ֨ית קָצִ֤ין חֶרְפָּתוֹ֙ ל֔וֹ בִּלְתִּ֥י חֶרְפָּת֖וֹ יָשִׁ֥יב לֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-yāśēm pānāyw lə-ʾiyyîm wə-lāḵaḏ rabbîm wə-hišbîṯ qāṣîn ḥerpāṯō lō biltî ḥerpāṯō yāšîḇ lō
verses.notes: **'Afterward he shall turn his face to the coastlands and shall take many of them; but a commander shall put an end to his insolence; indeed he shall turn his insolence back upon him.'** **= ROMAN INTERVENTION**: Antiochus III invaded Greece/Asia Minor (192-189 BCE); Rome under Lucius Cornelius Scipio Asiaticus defeated him at Magnesia (190 BCE). 'A commander' = Scipio. Treaty of Apamea (188 BCE) imposed massive indemnity. Qere-ketiv: וישב/וְיָשֵׂם.

verses.text: וְיָשֵׁ֣ב פָּנָ֔יו לְמָעוּזֵּ֖י אַרְצ֑וֹ וְנִכְשַׁ֥ל וְנָפַ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יִמָּצֵֽא׃
verses.translit: wə-yāšēḇ pānāyw lə-māʿūzzê ʾarṣō wə-niḵšal wə-nāp̄al wə-lōʾ yim-māṣēʾ
verses.notes: **'Then he shall turn his face back toward the fortresses of his own land; but he shall stumble and fall, and shall not be found.'** Antiochus III killed 187 BCE while raiding the temple of Bel at Elymais (per Diodorus 28.3; 29.15).

verses.text: וְעָמַ֧ד עַל־כַּנּ֛וֹ מַעֲבִ֥יר נוֹגֵ֖שׂ הֶ֣דֶר מַלְכ֑וּת וּבְיָמִ֤ים אֲחָדִים֙ יִשָּׁבֵ֔ר וְלֹ֥א בְאַפַּ֖יִם וְלֹ֥א בְמִלְחָמָֽה׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāmaḏ ʿal-kannō maʿăḇîr nōḡēś heḏer malḵūṯ ū-ḇə-yāmîm ʾăḥāḏîm yiš-šāḇēr wə-lōʾ ḇə-ʾappayim wə-lōʾ ḇə-milḥāmāh
verses.notes: **'Then shall arise in his place one who shall send an exactor of tribute through the glory of the kingdom; but within a few days he shall be broken, neither in anger nor in battle.'** **= SELEUCUS IV PHILOPATOR** (187-175 BCE), Antiochus III's eldest son. The 'exactor of tribute' = Heliodorus, his treasurer, sent to seize Jerusalem temple-funds (2 Macc 3). Seleucus IV was assassinated by Heliodorus in 175 BCE — 'broken, neither in anger nor in battle' = no public conflict.

verses.text: וְעָמַ֤ד עַל־כַּנּוֹ֙ נִבְזֶ֔ה וְלֹא־נָתְנ֥וּ עָלָ֖יו ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֑וּת וּבָ֣א בְשַׁלְוָ֔ה וְהֶחֱזִ֥יק מַלְכ֖וּת בַּחֲלַקְלַקּֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāmaḏ ʿal-kannō niḇzeh wə-lōʾ-nāṯənū ʿālāyw hōḏ malḵūṯ ū-ḇāʾ ḇə-šalwāh wə-heḥĕzîq malḵūṯ ba-ḥălaqlaqqōṯ
verses.notes: **'In his place shall arise a contemptible person to whom royal majesty has not been given; he shall come in without warning and obtain the kingdom by flatteries.'** **= ANTIOCHUS IV EPIPHANES** (175-164 BCE). 'Contemptible person' (נִבְזֶה niḇzeh) reflects the post-event Jewish judgment. Antiochus IV seized the throne by intrigue against the rightful heir Demetrius (held hostage in Rome) and the infant son of Seleucus IV (whom he later murdered). vv 21-45 are the Antiochus IV section. Cross-corpus to 11:21-45 (Maccabean apocalypse: 'contemptible person' = Antiochus IV Epiphanes per Collins 1993 Hermeneia).

verses.text: וּזְרֹע֥וֹת הַשֶּׁ֛טֶף יִשָּׁטְפ֥וּ מִלְּפָנָ֖יו וְיִשָּׁבֵ֑רוּ וְגַ֖ם נְגִ֥יד בְּרִֽית׃
verses.translit: ū-zərōʿōṯ haš-šeṭep̄ yiš-šāṭəp̄ū mil-lə-p̄ānāyw wə-yiš-šāḇērū wə-ḡam nəḡîḏ bərîṯ
verses.notes: **'Armies shall be utterly swept away before him and broken, and the prince of the covenant also.'** **'PRINCE OF THE COVENANT'** (נְגִיד בְּרִית nəḡîḏ bərîṯ) = ONIAS III, the legitimate Zadokite high priest, deposed by Antiochus IV in favor of his Hellenizing brother Jason, then murdered at Daphne in 171 BCE (2 Macc 4:33-38). This is the same 'anointed one cut off' of 9:26 per the Maccabean reading.

verses.text: וּמִן־הִֽתְחַבְּר֥וּת אֵלָ֖יו יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִרְמָ֑ה וְעָלָ֥ה וְעָצַ֖ם בִּמְעַט־גּֽוֹי׃
verses.translit: ū-min-hiṯ-ḥabbərūṯ ʾēlāyw yaʿăśeh mirmāh wə-ʿālāh wə-ʿāṣam bi-mʿaṭ-gōy
verses.notes: **'And from the time that an alliance is made with him he shall act deceitfully; and he shall become strong with a small people.'** Antiochus IV's typically deceitful diplomacy.

verses.text: בְּשַׁלְוָ֞ה וּבְמִשְׁמַנֵּ֣י מְדִינָה֮ יָבוֹא֒ וְעָשָׂ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־עָשׂ֤וּ אֲבֹתָיו֙ וַאֲב֣וֹת אֲבֹתָ֔יו בִּזָּ֧ה וְשָׁלָ֛ל וּרְכ֖וּשׁ לָהֶ֣ם יִבְז֑וֹר וְעַ֧ל מִבְצָרִ֛ים יְחַשֵּׁ֥ב מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֖יו וְעַד־עֵֽת׃
verses.translit: bə-šalwāh ū-ḇə-mišmannê mə-ḏînāh yāḇōʾ wə-ʿāśāh ʾăšer lōʾ-ʿāśū ʾăḇōṯāyw wa-ʾăḇōṯ ʾăḇōṯāyw biz-zāh wə-šālāl ū-rḵūš lā-hem yiḇzōr wə-ʿal miḇṣārîm yə-ḥaššēḇ maḥšəḇōṯāyw wə-ʿaḏ-ʿēṯ
verses.notes: **'Without warning he shall come into the richest parts of the province; and he shall do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers have done, scattering among them plunder, spoil, and goods. He shall devise plans against strongholds, but only for a time.'** Antiochus IV's distributing wealth to gain political support (Polybius 26.1.10-11; 31.4 — Polybius mocks him as 'Epimanes').

verses.text: וְיָעֵר֩ כֹּח֨וֹ וּלְבָב֜וֹ עַל־מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּגֶב֮ בְּחַ֣יִל גָּדוֹל֒ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֗גֶב יִתְגָּרֶה֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה בְּחַֽיִל־גָּד֥וֹל וְעָצ֖וּם עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֣א יַעֲמֹ֔ד כִּֽי־יַחְשְׁב֥וּ עָלָ֖יו מַחֲשָׁבֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: wə-yāʿēr kōḥō ū-ləḇāḇō ʿal-meleḵ han-neḡeḇ bə-ḥayil gāḏōl ū-meleḵ han-neḡeḇ yiṯgāreh lam-milḥāmāh bə-ḥayil-gāḏōl wə-ʿāṣūm ʿaḏ-məʾōḏ wə-lōʾ yaʿămōḏ kî-yaḥšəḇū ʿālāyw maḥăšāḇōṯ
verses.notes: **'He shall stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south shall wage war with a great and exceeding mighty army, but he shall not stand, for plots shall be devised against him.'** **= SIXTH SYRIAN WAR** (170-168 BCE): Antiochus IV invaded Ptolemaic Egypt. Ptolemy VI Philometor was the 'king of the south'. Polybius 28.18-23.

verses.text: וְאֹכְלֵ֧י פַת־בָּג֛וֹ יִשְׁבְּר֖וּהוּ וְחֵיל֣וֹ יִשְׁט֑וֹף וְנָפְל֖וּ חֲלָלִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃
verses.translit: wə-ʾōḵəlê p̄aṯ-bāḡō yišbərūhū wə-ḥêlō yišṭōp̄ wə-nāp̄əlū ḥălālîm rabbîm
verses.notes: **'Even those who eat his rich food shall be his undoing; his army shall be swept away, and many shall fall down slain.'** Treachery within Ptolemy VI's court — his own counselors betrayed him.

verses.text: וּשְׁנֵיהֶ֤ם הַמְּלָכִים֙ לְבָבָ֣ם לְמֵרָ֔ע וְעַל־שֻׁלְחָ֥ן אֶחָ֖ד כָּזָ֣ב יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְלֹ֣א תִצְלָ֔ח כִּי־ע֥וֹד קֵ֖ץ לַמּוֹעֵֽד׃
verses.translit: ū-šənêhem ham-məlāḵîm ləḇāḇām lə-mērāʿ wə-ʿal-šulḥān ʾeḥāḏ kāzāḇ yə-ḏabbērū wə-lōʾ ṯiṣlāḥ kî-ʿōḏ qēṣ lam-mōʿēḏ
verses.notes: **'And as for the two kings, their minds shall be bent on mischief; they shall speak lies at the same table, but to no avail; for the end is yet to be at the time appointed.'** Antiochus IV pretended to support Ptolemy VI while plotting; Memphis negotiations (169 BCE). 'The appointed time' = the eschatological end.

verses.text: וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אַרְצוֹ֙ בִּרְכ֣וּשׁ גָּד֔וֹל וּלְבָב֖וֹ עַל־בְּרִ֣ית קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְעָשָׂ֖ה וְשָׁ֥ב לְאַרְצֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-yāšōḇ ʾarṣō bi-rḵūš gāḏōl ū-ləḇāḇō ʿal-bərîṯ qōḏeš wə-ʿāśāh wə-šāḇ lə-ʾarṣō
verses.notes: **'And he shall return to his land with great substance, but his heart shall be set against the holy covenant. And he shall work his will, and return to his own land.'** Antiochus IV's return from his first Egyptian campaign (169 BCE), passing through Jerusalem and plundering the Temple (1 Macc 1:20-24; 2 Macc 5:11-21).

verses.text: לַמּוֹעֵ֥ד יָשׁ֖וּב וּבָ֣א בַנֶּ֑גֶב וְלֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה כָרִאשֹׁנָ֖ה וְכָאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃
verses.translit: lam-mōʿēḏ yāšūḇ ū-ḇāʾ ḇan-neḡeḇ wə-lōʾ-ṯihyeh ḵā-rîšōnāh wə-ḵā-ʾaḥărōnāh
verses.notes: **'At the time appointed he shall return and come into the south; but it shall not be this time as it was before.'** Antiochus IV's second Egyptian campaign (168 BCE).

verses.text: וּבָ֨אוּ ב֜וֹ צִיִּ֤ים כִּתִּים֙ וְנִכְאָ֔ה וְשָׁ֛ב וְזָעַ֥ם עַל־בְּרִֽית־ק֖וֹדֶשׁ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וְשָׁ֣ב וְיָבֵ֔ן עַל־עֹזְבֵ֖י בְּרִ֥ית קֹֽדֶשׁ׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇāʾū ḇō ṣiyyîm Kittîm wə-niḵʾāh wə-šāḇ wə-zāʿam ʿal-bərîṯ-qōḏeš wə-ʿāśāh wə-šāḇ wə-yāḇēn ʿal-ʿōzəḇê bərîṯ qōḏeš
verses.notes: **'For ships of Kittim shall come against him, and he shall be afraid and withdraw, and shall turn back and be enraged and take action against the holy covenant. He shall turn back and give heed to those who forsake the holy covenant.'** **= THE 'DAY OF ELEUSIS'** (168 BCE): Roman envoy Gaius Popillius Laenas drew a circle around Antiochus IV near Alexandria and demanded he leave Egypt — Antiochus complied (Polybius 29.27; Livy 45.12). **KITTIM** (כִּתִּים) = Cyprus/Romans by extension; the term in Qumran usage (1QpHab; 1QM) refers specifically to Romans. The humiliated Antiochus IV vented his rage on Jerusalem (167 BCE), beginning the persecution and the 'desolating sacrilege.'

verses.text: וּזְרֹעִ֖ים מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יַעֲמֹ֑דוּ וְחִלְּל֞וּ הַמִּקְדָּ֤שׁ הַמָּעוֹז֙ וְהֵסִ֣ירוּ הַתָּמִ֔יד וְנָתְנ֖וּ הַשִּׁקּ֥וּץ מְשׁוֹמֵֽם׃
verses.translit: ū-zərōʿîm mim-mennū yaʿămōḏū wə-ḥilləlū ham-miqdāš ham-māʿōz wə-hēsîrū hat-tāmîḏ wə-nāṯənū haš-šiqqūṣ mə-šōmēm
verses.notes: **'Forces from him shall appear and profane the temple and fortress, and shall take away the continual burnt offering. And they shall set up the abomination that makes desolate.'** **THE ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION** — הַשִּׁקּוּץ מְשׁוֹמֵם (haš-šiqqūṣ mə-šōmēm). **HISTORICAL FULFILLMENT**: 15 Kislev 167 BCE — altar to Zeus Olympios / Baal Shamayim erected on the Jerusalem temple altar (1 Macc 1:54: 'they erected a desolating sacrilege upon the altar of burnt offering'; 1 Macc 1:59 — pig sacrificed 25 Kislev). **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR NT**: Matt 24:15 + Mark 13:14: 'when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place — let the reader understand' — Jesus's Olivet discourse, with the explicit reading-instruction noting Daniel's prophetic-text status. 2 Thess 2:3-4 (the man of lawlessness 'takes his seat in the temple of God'). Cross-corpus to 11:31, 11:36 abomination + king-exalts-himself + 2 Thess 2:3-4 (man of lawlessness).

verses.text: וּמַרְשִׁיעֵ֣י בְרִ֔ית יַחֲנִ֖יף בַּחֲלַקּ֑וֹת וְעַ֛ם יֹדְעֵ֥י אֱלֹהָ֖יו יַחֲזִ֥קוּ וְעָשֽׂוּ׃
verses.translit: ū-maršîʿê ḇərîṯ yaḥănîp̄ ba-ḥălaqqōṯ wə-ʿam yōḏəʿê ʾĔlōhāyw yaḥăziqū wə-ʿāśū
verses.notes: **'He shall seduce with flattery those who violate the covenant; but the people who know their God shall stand firm and take action.'** The Hellenizing Jews (the *mityawanim* of 1 Macc 1:11-15) vs the Maccabean resistance and the proto-Hasidim/Hasideans (1 Macc 2:42; 1 Macc 7:13).

verses.text: וּמַשְׂכִּ֣ילֵי עָ֔ם יָבִ֖ינוּ לָֽרַבִּ֑ים וְנִכְשְׁל֞וּ בְּחֶ֧רֶב וּבְלֶהָבָ֛ה בִּשְׁבִ֥י וּבְבִזָּ֖ה יָמִֽים׃
verses.translit: ū-maśkîlê ʿām yāḇînū lā-rabbîm wə-niḵšəlū bə-ḥereḇ ū-ḇə-lehāḇāh bi-šḇî ū-ḇə-ḇizzāh yāmîm
verses.notes: **'And those among the people who are wise shall make many understand, though they shall fall by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder, for some days.'** **THE MASKILIM** (מַשְׂכִּילִים maśkîlîm 'the wise/insightful ones') — the teachers who pass on understanding during persecution. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. 12:3, 12:10 (the maśkîlîm shine like stars); this group is widely identified as the proto-Hasidim / proto-Qumran group OR the Daniel-authorship circle itself (Collins 1993). The Qumran community used משכיל as a leadership title (1QS 3:13, 9:12-21).

verses.text: וּבְהִכָּ֣שְׁלָ֔ם יֵעָזְר֖וּ עֵ֣זֶר מְעָ֑ט וְנִלְו֧וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם רַבִּ֖ים בַּחֲלַקְלַקּֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇə-hik-kāšəlām yē-ʿāzərū ʿēzer məʿāṭ wə-nilwū ʿălêhem rabbîm ba-ḥălaqlaqqōṯ
verses.notes: **'When they fall, they shall receive a little help, and many shall join themselves to them with flattery.'** **'A LITTLE HELP'** = the Maccabean armed-resistance — per Collins 1993, the Daniel author (a *maskil*) is somewhat ambivalent about the Maccabees, viewing them as marginally helpful but not the eschatological deliverers. Compare to 1 Macc's pro-Maccabean apologetic.

verses.text: וּמִן־הַמַּשְׂכִּילִ֣ים יִכָּֽשְׁל֗וּ לִצְר֥וֹף בָּהֶ֛ם וּלְבָרֵ֥ר וְלַלְבֵּ֖ן עַד־עֵ֣ת קֵ֑ץ כִּי־ע֖וֹד לַמּוֹעֵֽד׃
verses.translit: ū-min-ham-maśkîlîm yik-kāšəlū liṣ-rōp̄ bā-hem ū-lə-ḇārēr wə-lal-bēn ʿaḏ-ʿēṯ qēṣ kî-ʿōḏ lam-mōʿēḏ
verses.notes: **'And some of the wise shall fall, to refine and to cleanse them and to make them white, until the time of the end; for it is yet for the time appointed.'** **PURIFICATION-THROUGH-PERSECUTION**: the maskilim's martyrdoms have refining purpose. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Mal 3:2-3 (refiner's fire); cf. 1 Pet 1:7 (faith tested by fire); cf. Rev 7:14 (those who 'washed their robes... in the blood of the lamb'). 'Time of the end' = the imminent eschatological denouement.

verses.text: וְעָשָׂ֨ה כִרְצוֹנ֜וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְיִתְרוֹמֵ֤ם וְיִתְגַּדֵּל֙ עַל־כָּל־אֵ֔ל וְעַל֙ אֵ֣ל אֵלִ֔ים יְדַבֵּ֖ר נִפְלָא֑וֹת וְהִצְלִ֙יחַ֙ עַד־כָּ֣לָה זַ֔עַם כִּ֥י נֶחֱרָצָ֖ה נֶעֱשָֽׂתָה׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāśāh ḵi-rṣōnō ham-meleḵ wə-yiṯrōmēm wə-yiṯgaddēl ʿal-kol-ʾēl wə-ʿal ʾēl ʾēlîm yə-ḏabbēr nip̄lāʾōṯ wə-hiṣlîaḥ ʿaḏ-kālāh zaʿam kî neḥĕrāṣāh neʿĕśāṯāh
verses.notes: **'And the king shall do according to his will; he shall exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak astonishing things against the God of gods. He shall prosper till the indignation is accomplished; for what is determined shall be done.'** **THE KING EXALTS HIMSELF**: Antiochus IV's self-divinization (his epithet 'Epiphanes' = 'manifest [god]'; coins styled him *theos epiphanes*). **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: 2 Thess 2:3-4 — 'the man of lawlessness... who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God' — direct Dan 11:36 paraphrase. cf. Rev 13:5-6 (the beast utters blasphemies); cf. 7:25, 8:11. Cross-corpus to 11:36 king-exalts-himself + 2 Thess 2:3-4 (man of lawlessness).

verses.text: וְעַל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יָבִ֔ין וְעַל־חֶמְדַּ֥ת נָשִׁ֛ים וְעַל־כָּל־אֱל֖וֹהַּ לֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין כִּ֥י עַל־כֹּ֖ל יִתְגַּדָּֽל׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿal-ʾĕlōhê ʾăḇōṯāyw lōʾ yāḇîn wə-ʿal-ḥemdaṯ nāšîm wə-ʿal-kol-ʾĕlōah lōʾ yāḇîn kî ʿal-kōl yiṯgaddāl
verses.notes: **'He shall give no heed to the gods of his fathers, or to the one beloved by women; he shall not give heed to any other god, for he shall magnify himself above all.'** **'BELOVED BY WOMEN'** (חֶמְדַּת נָשִׁים ḥemdaṯ nāšîm): commonly identified as Tammuz/Adonis (cf. Ezek 8:14 'women weeping for Tammuz') — Antiochus IV neglected traditional Seleucid Adonis-worship in favor of Olympian Zeus. Alternative readings: Dionysus, or 'the desire of women' as messianic-figure (rabbinic + dispensationalist readings).

verses.text: וְלֶאֱלֹ֙הַּ֙ מָֽעֻזִּ֔ים עַל־כַּנּ֖וֹ יְכַבֵּ֑ד וְלֶאֱל֜וֹהַּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יְדָעֻ֣הוּ אֲבֹתָ֗יו יְכַבֵּ֛ד בְּזָהָ֧ב וּבְכֶ֛סֶף וּבְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָ֖ה וּבַחֲמֻדֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: wə-le-ʾĕlōah māʿuzzîm ʿal-kannō yə-ḵabbēḏ wə-le-ʾĕlōah ʾăšer lōʾ-yəḏāʿuhū ʾăḇōṯāyw yə-ḵabbēḏ bə-zāhāḇ ū-ḇə-ḵesep̄ ū-ḇə-ʾeḇen yəqārāh ū-ḇa-ḥămuḏōṯ
verses.notes: **'He shall honor the god of fortresses instead of these; a god whom his fathers did not know he shall honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.'** **'GOD OF FORTRESSES'** (אֱלוֹהַּ מָעֻזִּים ʾĕlōah māʿuzzîm) = Zeus Olympios / Jupiter Capitolinus, whom Antiochus IV especially honored — at his great festival at Daphne (166 BCE per Polybius 30.25-26).

verses.text: וְעָשָׂ֞ה לְמִבְצְרֵ֤י מָֽעֻזִּים֙ עִם־אֱל֣וֹהַּ נֵכָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הכיר יַכִּ֖יר יַרְבֶּ֣ה כָב֑וֹד וְהִמְשִׁילָם֙ בָּֽרַבִּ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה יְחַלֵּ֥ק בִּמְחִֽיר׃
verses.translit: wə-ʿāśāh lə-miḇṣərê māʿuzzîm ʿim-ʾĕlōah nēḵār ʾăšer yakkîr yarbeh ḵāḇōḏ wə-himšîlām bā-rabbîm wa-ʾăḏāmāh yə-ḥallēq bi-mḥîr
verses.notes: **'He shall deal with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign god; those who acknowledge him he shall magnify with honor. He shall make them rulers over many and shall divide the land for a price.'** Antiochus IV's policy of installing pro-Seleucid Hellenizers (Jason, Menelaus, Alcimus) in high-priestly + civic positions. Qere-ketiv: הכיר/יַכִּיר. End of the verifiable historical sequence; vv 40-45 contain unfulfilled prediction.

verses.text: וּבְעֵ֣ת קֵ֗ץ יִתְנַגַּ֤ח עִמּוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַנֶּ֔גֶב וְיִשְׂתָּעֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו מֶ֣לֶךְ הַצָּפ֗וֹן בְּרֶ֙כֶב֙ וּבְפָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וּבָאֳנִיּ֖וֹת רַבּ֑וֹת וּבָ֥א בַאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְשָׁטַ֥ף וְעָבָֽר׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇə-ʿēṯ qēṣ yiṯnaggaḥ ʿimmō meleḵ han-neḡeḇ wə-yiśtāʿēr ʿālāyw meleḵ haṣ-ṣāp̄ōn bə-reḵeḇ ū-ḇə-pārāšîm ū-ḇo-ʾŏniyyōṯ rabbōṯ ū-ḇāʾ ḇa-ʾărāṣōṯ wə-šāṭap̄ wə-ʿāḇār
verses.notes: **'At the time of the end the king of the south shall attack him; but the king of the north shall rush upon him like a whirlwind, with chariots and horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall come into countries and shall overflow and pass through.'** **vv 40-45: GENUINE UNFULFILLED PREDICTION** — Collins 1993 + scholarly consensus: this final invasion of Egypt did not occur. Antiochus IV's actual end (164 BCE) was on campaign in PERSIA (the east), not Egypt (the south). This discrepancy is the foundational scholarly argument for dating the text precisely to 167-164 BCE: composed during the persecution, before Antiochus's actual death made the prediction falsifiable.

verses.text: וּבָא֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַצְּבִ֔י וְרַבּ֖וֹת יִכָּשֵׁ֑לוּ וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יִמָּלְט֣וּ מִיָּד֔וֹ אֱד֣וֹם וּמוֹאָ֔ב וְרֵאשִׁ֖ית בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇāʾ bə-ʾereṣ haṣ-ṣəḇî wə-rabbōṯ yik-kāšēlū wə-ʾēlleh yim-māləṭū mî-yāḏō ʾĔḏōm ū-Mōʾāḇ wə-rēʾšîṯ bənê ʿAmmōn
verses.notes: **'He shall come into the glorious land. And tens of thousands shall fall, but these shall be delivered out of his hand: Edom and Moab and the main part of the Ammonites.'** Edom + Moab + Ammon were traditional Israelite-enemy nations who would, per the prediction, escape the catastrophe. Some commentators interpret these as figurative for non-Israel.

verses.text: וְיִשְׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ בַּאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה לִפְלֵיטָֽה׃
verses.translit: wə-yišlaḥ yāḏō ba-ʾărāṣōṯ wə-ʾereṣ Miṣrayim lōʾ ṯihyeh lip̄lêṭāh
verses.notes: **'He shall stretch out his hand against the countries, and the land of Egypt shall not escape.'**

verses.text: וּמָשַׁ֗ל בְּמִכְמַנֵּי֙ הַזָּהָ֣ב וְהַכֶּ֔סֶף וּבְכֹ֖ל חֲמֻד֣וֹת מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֻבִ֥ים וְכֻשִׁ֖ים בְּמִצְעָדָֽיו׃
verses.translit: ū-māšal bə-miḵmannê haz-zāhāḇ wə-hak-kesep̄ ū-ḇə-ḵōl ḥămuḏōṯ Miṣrāyim wə-Luḇîm wə-Ḵušîm bə-miṣʿāḏāyw
verses.notes: **'He shall become ruler of the treasures of gold and of silver, and all the precious things of Egypt; and the Libyans and the Ethiopians shall follow in his train.'**

verses.text: וּשְׁמֻע֣וֹת יְבַהֲלֻ֔הוּ מִמִּזְרָ֖ח וּמִצָּפ֑וֹן וְיָצָא֙ בְּחֵמָ֣א גְדֹלָ֔ה לְהַשְׁמִ֥יד וּֽלְהַחֲרִ֖ים רַבִּֽים׃
verses.translit: ū-šəmuʿōṯ yə-ḇahăluhū mim-mizrāḥ ū-miṣ-ṣāp̄ōn wə-yāṣāʾ bə-ḥēmāʾ ḡəḏōlāh lə-hašmîḏ ū-lə-haḥărîm rabbîm
verses.notes: **'But tidings from the east and the north shall alarm him, and he shall go forth with great fury to exterminate and utterly destroy many.'** **HISTORICAL CONNECTION**: Antiochus IV did indeed head east in 165 BCE (Parthian threat, eastern revolts) and died there — but not in the manner this verse predicts. The prediction's east-and-north combination did not exactly match the historical event.

verses.text: וְיִטַּע֙ אָהֳלֶ֣י אַפַּדְנ֔וֹ בֵּ֥ין יַמִּ֖ים לְהַר־צְבִי־קֹ֑דֶשׁ וּבָא֙ עַד־קִצּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֥ין עוֹזֵ֖ר לֽוֹ׃
verses.translit: wə-yiṭṭaʿ ʾŏhŏlê ʾappaḏnō bên yammîm lə-har-ṣəḇî-qōḏeš ū-ḇāʾ ʿaḏ-qiṣṣō wə-ʾên ʿōzēr lō
verses.notes: **'And he shall pitch his palatial tents between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, with none to help him.'** **TERM**: אַפַּדְנוֹ (ʾappaḏnō 'his palace-tent') — Persian loanword *apadāna* (the columned-hall of Persian palaces). **THE PREDICTION**: Antiochus IV's final encampment between the sea (Mediterranean) and the Jerusalem temple-mount — and there meeting his end. **HISTORICAL OUTCOME**: Antiochus IV actually died at Tabae in Persia (Polybius 31.9), nowhere near Jerusalem. The discrepancy is the central evidence for the 167-164 BCE composition-window. The chapter ends with the anticipated death of the persecutor — setting up ch 12's resurrection prophecy.
